newsitem.title: RWANDA: U.N. refugee agency resuming work in Zaire camps.
newsitem.headline: U.N. refugee agency resuming work in Zaire camps.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency said on Friday it was resuming work in Rwandan refugee camps in Zaire suspended when Hutu refugees failed to cooperate with a census, but there were no immediate plans to restart the census effort.
Refugees had said they feared that indelible ink used by census takers would sterilise and poison them after what aid workers said was a rumour campaign by Hutu hardliners.
Aid workers said Hutu refugees also feared the ink would mean they could be detected by Rwandan government troops of the Tutsi-led army if they were forced into Rwanda.
Many of the estimated 1.1 million Rwandan Hutu refugees in Zaire and nearly 600,000 in Tanzania refuse to go home for fear of reprisals for Rwanda's genocide of up to a million people in 1994.
The U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) said on Thursday the 750,000 refugees in the Goma area camps could face serious food shortages because of their refusal to take part in the census.
"Donor countries are warning that they will not fund further food supplies to the camps until an accurate count of the refugees has been carried out," WFP said in a statement.
"Everything will be back to normal and operational by Monday," said Paul Stromberg, spokesman for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in Rwanda's capital Kigali.

"Our people are gradually going back into the camps so the suspension of operations is now over. We have not announced a restart of the census operations and I do not think we will try and start it again under the same terms," he added on Friday.
UNHCR suspended all non-emergency work for a week on Sunday because of failure to respond to the census.
The boycott shocked the U.N. refugee agency, which had been assured by refugee leaders that camp inmates would cooperate.

"The problem of the camps is not the registration operation so much as the political situation," said Stromberg, adding that UNHCR was prepared for an exodus of refugees from neighbouring Burundi in case of widespread continued violence between Hutus and Tutsis there.
UNHCR said the census was not designed to single out any refugees but was essential to allocate funds for aid in the face of falling interest among Western donors.
